topic: How does the 14.6% bandwidth affect frequency planning for multi-satellite networks with adjacent channel interference risks?
consensus_response: The 14.6% bandwidth in the Ku band affects frequency planning by increasing adjacent channel interference risks due to Doppler shift effects on frequency stability as satellites move. This reduces the number of orthogonal channels available, decreasing data rate and capacity. To mitigate this, advanced signal processing techniques like Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be integrated into existing design methods for optimal performance. By optimizing frequency allocation, orbit planning, and channel assignment, ML/AI can minimize interference in multi-satellite networks while balancing trade-offs between data rate, capacity, and interference.
reference_context: The regulatory community has allocated a wide range of frequencies for services that support Inter-Satellite Communication (ISC) for various applications, making it not necessary to pursue new frequency allocations since existing spectrum should suffice to meet expected demands till 2020.
